title: Hedging and Precision Language

topic_snapshot.description: Crucial language for making claims more accurate, academic, and less absolute (Band 7+ requirement). Avoiding sweeping generalizations.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Used when stating an opinion or belief that you think can be shown to be true.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: She is arguably the greatest athlete of her generation.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A balanced scale showing a strong argument outweighing a weaker one, representing a defensible opinion.

key_vocabulary_bank.example: The audience at the concert was predominantly young teenagers.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A crowd of people where the vast majority are wearing blue shirts, highlighting the concept of 'mostly'.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Seeming likely to be true, or able to be believed.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: It is entirely plausible that artificial intelligence will replace certain routine administrative jobs.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A person nodding thoughtfully while reviewing a realistic and logical plan on a document.

collocation_builder.meaning: Almost everyone or everything in a group (more precise than 'all').
collocation_builder.example: A vast majority of the respondents indicated that they prefer flexible working hours.

collocation_builder.meaning: Very improbable (softer and more academic than 'impossible').
collocation_builder.example: It is highly unlikely that a single solution will resolve the complex issue of climate change.

collocation_builder.meaning: To be likely to behave in a particular way or have a particular characteristic.
collocation_builder.example: People tend to be more productive when they work in a well-lit environment.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: It is widely believed that / A vast majority argue that
upgrade_section.example: It is widely believed that physical education is crucial for child development.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: This is highly likely to result in / This may potentially trigger
upgrade_section.example: Ignoring environmental policies is highly likely to result in irreversible ecological damage.

upgrade_section.better_upgrade: It is highly improbable / It seems unlikely
upgrade_section.example: It is highly improbable that global eradication of poverty can be achieved within a single decade.

sentence_frames: It is generally accepted that [Subject] tends to...
While it is plausible that [A], it is highly unlikely that [B].
A significant proportion of society arguably benefits from...

ielts_usage_examples.writing_example: While strict censorship may arguably prevent the spread of misinformation, it is highly unlikely to be effective in an era dominated by decentralized social media.
ielts_usage_examples.speaking_example: I'd say people predominantly consume news through their smartphones nowadays, as it tends to be far more convenient than buying a physical newspaper.

common_mistakes: Using absolute terms like 'All people', 'Always', or 'Never' which makes arguments vulnerable and lowers the Task Response score.
Using 'majority of' without 'the' or 'a' (e.g., writing 'Majority of people' instead of 'The majority of people').

quiz.question: Which of the following sentences uses appropriate academic hedging?

options.B: Nobody talks face-to-face anymore because of smartphones.
options.C: Heavy reliance on smartphones tends to diminish face-to-face interaction.
options.D: Smartphones will definitely destroy human relationships entirely.

quiz.explanation: Option C uses 'tends to' to hedge the claim, avoiding the absolute, generalized statements found in A, B, and D, which are penalized in IELTS.

quiz.question: Which word is a C1-level synonym for 'mostly' or 'mainly'?
quiz.explanation: 'Predominantly' is an excellent academic adverb to express that something consists mostly or primarily of a particular element.
